Direct fetches of fasb.org return HTTP 403 in this environment, so the ASU text was read through the search provider's rendering and is corroborated independently by the FASB's own ASU 2018-03. Still OPEN: whether the UK filing route publishes a filing TIME and not only a date (the FCA NSM API host answered HTTP 403 to every request here); T-R needs a timestamp. description: Settle the three named verification gaps that were on the critical path: the UK filing-timestamp question, the IFRS 18 day-level instrument dates, and the linguistic-distance measure choice
data_version: research/event_calendar.csv, research/panel_v1.2.csv, research/decision_log.md (D-021, D-022, D-023), research/source_ledger.csv (S-60 to S-71)
key_finding: All three gaps are now closed or determined from primary sources. (a) The FCA National Storage Mechanism publishes a filing DATE, not a time: the published glossary and the Investor User Guide define both fields as dates, while the PIP-to-NSM schema carries a mandatory PublishingDate timestamp that binds PIPs only from 3 November 2025. CONSEQUENCE: the two retrospective UK events cannot be timed at all, because their transition windows (2016-01-01, 2019-01-01) precede the timestamp regime; the UK stays viable for PH-1. The NSM search API answered HTTP 403, so the condition is UNVERIFIED, not false, and a failed retrieval is recorded as a failed retrieval. (b) The IFRS 18 instruments are pinned: EU T-A 2026-02-13 (endorsement) with OJ publication 2026-02-16; UK T-A 2025-12-10 (UKEB formal adoption, closing the gap v1.2 left open); Saudi T-A 2024-12-26 (SOCPA adoption) with the CMA early-adoption decision of 2026-06-30 recorded separately, because v1.2 had registered the early-adoption date as the mandatory-adoption date. The Saudi conflict is recorded, not resolved, together with its consequence: the CMA-mandated pre-adoption impact disclosure falls inside the Saudi transition window, so Saudi has no clean T-PRE anchor and its standing in PH-1 is an open design question to be settled before the holdout opens. (c) The published S-44 index (Joshi and Lahiri 2015 friction index over 192 WALS features) cannot be reproduced exactly panel-wide, because Ethnologue is licensed and versioned, the merge was manual, and Table 1 covers only the paper's 84-country 2004-2018 sample; the registered fallback ordinal scale is therefore selected by the rule, with the published values kept as an external validation of the ordering, and the fallback's category boundaries remain to be enumerated by dated decision before the holdout opens
notes: No outcome-period return was computed or inspected. The IFRS 18 events are registered in research/panel_v1.2.csv and deliberately NOT in the retrospective event calendar, because adding 2024-2026 rows would destroy the calendar's defining property (every retrospective event has T-A on or before 2017-10-31, so the chronological holdout split is empty; D-014)
